records.literal_gloss: For the director. Of David. To bring to remembrance.

en.L: For the director: of David; to bring to remembrance.
en.B: For the music director. Of David. For remembrance.
en.R: For the leader of the music. By David. To call to mind.

fr.L: Au chef de chœur : de David ; pour faire souvenir.
fr.B: Au chef de chœur. De David. Pour faire mémoire.
fr.R: Pour le chef des musiciens. De David. Pour rappeler à Dieu.

sw.L: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya: ya Daudi; kwa kukumbusha.
sw.B: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya. Ya Daudi. Kwa ukumbusho.
sw.R: Kwa kiongozi wa waimbaji. Ya Daudi. Kwa kumkumbusha Mungu.

es.L: Al director del coro: de David; para hacer recordar.
es.B: Al director del coro. De David. Para recordar.
es.R: Para el director de la música. De David. Para traer a la memoria.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: to bring to remembrance: to call to mind before God
decisions.reason: As in 38:1, the only other psalm with this heading. The psalm may call the sufferer's need to God's mind, or may have been sung with the "memorial portion" of the grain offering ('azkarah, Leviticus 2:2), a word from the same root.

decisions.choice: Psalm 70 is Psalm 40:14-18
decisions.reason: Verses 2-6 repeat Psalm 40:14-18 with small changes: several times "God" stands where Psalm 40 has the divine name, and the other way round in verse 6. Psalms 42-83 often use "God" ('elohim) where other psalms use the name, and each level here follows the word this psalm has.

decisions.choice: By David; To call to mind
alternatives: Of David; To bring to remembrance
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words, as in 38:1; the sense of the phrase is uncertain (m3).

decisions.choice: "Pour rappeler à Dieu" at Readable
decisions.reason: French "rappeler" needs to say to whom; the title asks that the psalmist's need be brought to God's mind (meaning decision m3), so Readable names God.

decisions.choice: "Kwa kumkumbusha Mungu" (to remind God) at Readable
decisions.reason: The Swahili verb needs an object, and the meaning decision reads the heading as calling the sufferer's need to mind before God; Readable names God as the one reminded.

records.literal_gloss: God, to deliver me; YHWH, to my help hurry.

en.L: God, [come] to rescue me; \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hurry to my help!
en.B: God, come and rescue me! \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, be quick to help me!
en.R: God, come and save me! \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hurry and help me!

fr.L: Ô Dieu, [viens] me délivrer ; \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, hâte-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de me secourir !
fr.B: Ô Dieu, viens me délivrer ! \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, viens vite à mon secours !
fr.R: Dieu, viens me sauver ! \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, dépêche-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de m’aider !

sw.L: Ee Mungu, [uje] kuniokoa; \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ufanye haraka kunisaidia!
sw.B: Ee Mungu, uje uniokoe! \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uharakishe kunisaidia!
sw.R: Mungu, njoo uniokoe! \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, fanya haraka unisaidie!

es.L: Oh Dios, [ven] a librarme; \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡apresúrate a socorrerme!
es.B: ¡Oh Dios, ven a rescatarme! \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡date prisa en ayudarme!
es.R: ¡Dios, ven y sálvame! \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡ven pronto a ayudarme!

decisions.choice: God, to deliver me: a cry with the verb left out
alternatives: God, be pleased to deliver me (Psalm 40:14)
decisions.reason: The first line has no main verb, only "to deliver me". Psalm 40:14 begins "Be pleased, YHWH, to deliver me"; here the urgent cry is shorter, and "hurry" at the end of the verse governs both halves.

decisions.choice: Psalm 40:14
decisions.reason: This verse matches Psalm 40:14, with "God" in place of the first "YHWH".

decisions.choice: come
decisions.reason: The cry lacks a verb; "come" is supplied from the sense and from "hurry" in the second half. Literal marks it with brackets.

source.text: יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ וְיַחְפְּרוּ֮ מְבַקְשֵׁ֪י נַ֫פְשִׁ֥י יִסֹּ֣גוּ אָ֭חוֹר וְיִכָּלְמ֑וּ חֲ֝פֵצֵ֗י רָעָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: May they be ashamed and abashed, those who seek my life; may they be turned back and humiliated, those who desire my harm.

en.L: May they be ashamed and abashed, those who seek my life; \q may they be turned back and humiliated, \q those who desire my harm.
en.B: Let those who are out to take my life be shamed and confounded; \q let those who want me hurt be driven back in disgrace.
en.R: Some people want me dead. Let them be ashamed and confused. \q Some people want to see me hurt. \q Make them turn away in shame.

fr.L: Qu’ils soient honteux et confus, ceux qui cherchent ma vie ; \q qu’ils reculent et soient humiliés, \q ceux qui désirent mon malheur.
fr.B: Que ceux qui en veulent à ma vie soient couverts de honte et de confusion ; \q que ceux qui souhaitent mon malheur reculent, déshonorés.
fr.R: Certains veulent ma mort. Qu’ils aient honte et soient confus. \q Certains veulent me voir souffrir. \q Fais-les reculer, pleins de honte.

sw.L: Waaibike na kufadhaika wale wanaoutafuta uhai wangu; \q warudishwe nyuma na kufedheheka, \q wale wapendao madhara yangu.
sw.B: Wale wanaotaka kuniua na waaibishwe na kuchanganyikiwa; \q wale wanaotaka niumie na warudishwe nyuma kwa fedheha.
sw.R: Watu fulani wanataka nife. Na waone aibu na kuchanganyikiwa. \q Watu fulani wanataka kuniona nikiumia. \q Uwafanye warudi nyuma kwa aibu.

es.L: Que sean avergonzados y confundidos los que buscan mi vida; \q que retrocedan y sean humillados \q los que desean mi mal.
es.B: Que queden en vergüenza y confusión los que quieren quitarme la vida; \q que los que desean mi daño retrocedan avergonzados.
es.R: Hay quienes me quieren muerto. Que queden avergonzados y confundidos. \q Hay quienes quieren verme sufrir. \q Haz que se vuelvan atrás llenos de vergüenza.

decisions.choice: may they be ashamed: a prayer against enemies
decisions.reason: The verbs are wishes: that the enemies' plans fail and the shame they meant for him falls on them (35:4, 26; 40:15).

decisions.choice: seek my life: try to kill me
decisions.reason: As in 40:15, which adds "to snatch it away" and "together"; this verse is shorter.

decisions.choice: Let them ... Make them ...
decisions.reason: Readable puts the wishes as plain requests, with the enemies named first.

records.literal_gloss: May they turn back on account of their shame, those who say, Aha, aha!

en.L: May they turn back on account of their shame, \q those who say, "Aha! Aha!"
en.B: Let those who crow "Aha! Aha!" \q retreat because of their own disgrace.
en.R: Some people laugh and say, "Ha! Ha!" \q Let them run away because they are put to shame.

fr.L: Qu’ils reculent à cause de leur honte, \q ceux qui disent : « Ah ! ah ! »
fr.B: Que ceux qui ricanent : « Ah ! ah ! » \q battent en retraite à cause de leur propre honte.
fr.R: Certains rient et disent : « Ha ! ha ! » \q Qu’ils s’enfuient, couverts de honte.

sw.L: Warudi nyuma kwa sababu ya aibu yao, \q wale wasemao, "Aha! Aha!"
sw.B: Wale wanaoshangilia, "Aha! Aha!" \q na warudi nyuma kwa sababu ya fedheha yao wenyewe.
sw.R: Watu fulani hucheka na kusema, "Ha! Ha!" \q Na wakimbie kwa sababu wameaibishwa.

es.L: Que se vuelvan atrás a causa de su vergüenza \q los que dicen: «¡Ajá! ¡Ajá!».
es.B: Que los que gritan «¡Ajá! ¡Ajá!» \q retrocedan por su propia deshonra.
es.R: Hay quienes se ríen y dicen: «¡Ja! ¡Ja!». \q Que huyan, porque han quedado en vergüenza.

decisions.choice: Aha, aha: a gloating laugh
decisions.reason: The cry is the glee of enemies at someone's fall (35:21, 25; 40:16).

decisions.choice: turn back: retreat, as an army turns and runs
decisions.reason: Psalm 40:16 has "be appalled" (shamem); this verse has "turn back" (shuv), repeating the picture of defeat from verse 3.

decisions.choice: on account of their shame: as the result of it
decisions.reason: The word ('eqev) means "as the consequence of": their own shame drives them off.

source.text: יָ֘שִׂ֤ישׂוּ וְיִשְׂמְח֨וּ׀בְּךָ֗ כָּֽל־מְבַ֫קְשֶׁ֥יךָ וְיֹאמְר֣וּ תָ֭מִיד יִגְדַּ֣ל אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֹ֝הֲבֵ֗י יְשׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: May they exult and rejoice in you, all who seek you; and may they say continually, Great [is] God, those who love your salvation.

en.L: May they exult and rejoice in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, all who seek {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q and may they say continually, "Great [is] God!" \q those who love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation.
en.B: But may all who look for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be glad and take delight in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q and let all who love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saving help keep saying, "God is great!"
en.R: But let all who come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be happy and full of joy because of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Let all who love it when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save them say again and again, "God is great!"

fr.L: Qu’ils exultent et se réjouissent en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cherchent ; \q et qu’ils disent continuellement : « Grand [est] Dieu ! », \q ceux qui aiment {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} salut.
fr.B: Mais que tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cherchent soient dans la joie et trouvent en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} leur bonheur, \q et que ceux qui aiment {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} secours ne cessent de dire : « Dieu est grand ! »
fr.R: Mais que tous ceux qui viennent à {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} soient heureux et pleins de joie grâce à {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. \q Que tous ceux qui aiment être sauvés par {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} disent sans arrêt : « Dieu est grand ! »

sw.L: Washangilie na kufurahi ndani {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} wote wakutafutao; \q na waseme daima, "Mungu [ni] mkuu!" \q wale waupendao wokovu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.B: Lakini wote wanaokutafuta na wafurahi na kukushangilia {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, \q na wote waupendao msaada {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kuokoa waseme daima, "Mungu ni mkuu!"
sw.R: Lakini wote wanaokuja kwako na wawe na furaha tele kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. \q Wote wanaopenda {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unapowaokoa waseme tena na tena, "Mungu ni mkuu!"

es.L: Que se regocijen y se alegren en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} todos los que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} buscan; \q y que digan continuamente: «¡Grande [es] Dios!», \q los que aman {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} salvación.
es.B: Pero que todos los que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} buscan se alegren y se gocen en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q y que todos los que aman {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ayuda salvadora digan siempre: «¡Dios es grande!».
es.R: Pero que todos los que vienen a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} estén felices y llenos de alegría por {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. \q Que todos los que se alegran cuando {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} los salvas digan una y otra vez: «¡Dios es grande!».

decisions.choice: Great is God: praise, or a wish
decisions.reason: The verb can be read as a wish, "may God be great", that is, be shown and praised as great. Psalm 40:17 has the divine name here.

decisions.choice: those who seek you: those who turn to God in worship and prayer
decisions.reason: To seek God is to come to him for help and to worship him (9:11; 24:6).

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: The wish for those who seek God is set against the wish for the enemies.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֤י׀עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְיוֹן֮ אֱלֹהִ֪ים חֽוּשָׁ֫ה־לִּ֥י עֶזְרִ֣י וּמְפַלְטִ֣י אַ֑תָּה יְ֝הוָ֗ה אַל־תְּאַחַֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I [am] afflicted and needy; God, hurry to me; my help and my deliverer [are] you; YHWH, do not delay.

en.L: But I [am] poor and needy; God, hurry to me! \q My help and my deliverer [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do not delay!
en.B: As for me, I am poor and in need; God, come to me quickly! \q You are my helper and the one who sets me free; \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do not hold back!
en.R: I am poor and I have nothing. God, come to me quickly! \q You are the one who helps me and saves me. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please do not wait!

fr.L: Mais moi, [je suis] humilié et indigent ; ô Dieu, hâte-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} vers moi ! \q Mon secours et mon libérateur, [c’est] {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ne tarde pas !
fr.B: Quant à moi, je suis pauvre et dans le besoin ; ô Dieu, viens vite vers moi ! \q C’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui m’aides et qui me libères ; \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} fais pas attendre !
fr.R: Je suis pauvre et je n’ai rien. Dieu, viens vite vers moi ! \q C’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui m’aides et me sauves. \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, s’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît, n’attends pas !

sw.L: Lakini mimi [ni] maskini na mhitaji; Ee Mungu, unijie upesi! \q Msaada wangu na mwokozi wangu [ni] {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}; \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, usikawie!
sw.B: Lakini mimi ni maskini na mhitaji; Ee Mungu, uje kwangu haraka! \q Wewe ndiwe msaidizi wangu na mkombozi wangu; \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, usichelewe!
sw.R: Mimi ni maskini na sina kitu. Mungu, njoo kwangu upesi! \q Wewe ndiye unayenisaidia na kuniokoa. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali usikawie!

es.L: Pero yo [soy] pobre y necesitado; ¡oh Dios, apresúrate a venir a mí! \q Mi ayuda y mi libertador [eres] {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}; \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡no {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} tardes!
es.B: En cuanto a mí, soy pobre y necesitado; ¡oh Dios, ven pronto a mí! \q Tú eres mi ayuda y el que me pone en libertad; \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡no {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} detengas!
es.R: Soy pobre y no tengo nada. ¡Dios, ven pronto a mí! \q Tú eres el que me ayuda y me salva. \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡por favor, no esperes más!

decisions.choice: afflicted and needy: helpless and dependent on God
decisions.reason: As in 40:18; the pair describes those who have no help but God.

decisions.choice: Psalm 40:18
decisions.reason: Psalm 40:18 has "the Lord will think of me" where this verse has "God, hurry to me", and "my God" where this verse has the divine name. The psalm ends as it began, with "hurry" (verse 2).

decisions.choice: "maskini na mhitaji" for the afflicted and needy pair, the words of the terms note
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew words describe someone with no help but God. "Maskini" is the word that comes first to a Swahili reader for the first of the pair here; "mnyonge" (the lowly, the oppressed) serves where the English says "afflicted" alone.

decisions.choice: pobre y necesitado
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pair 'ani and 'evyon names someone poor and helpless who has only God to depend on. Spanish uses "pobre" and "necesitado", the words used for this pair throughout the Psalms.
